entities.name: Pavlo Polubotok
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pavlo Polubotok, a prominent Ukrainian Cossack leader, assumed the critical role of Acting Hetman of Left-bank Ukraine from 1722 until his death in 1724, at a pivotal moment when the autonomous Cossack Hetmanate faced escalating encroachment from the Russian Empire under Peter the Great. His brief but impactful tenure was defined by a principled and ultimately tragic struggle to preserve the traditional liberties and self-governance of the Ukrainian Cossacks against the centralized absolutism of the Russian Tsar. Polubotok's actions, particularly his defiant stand against imperial overreach, solidified his image as a national hero and a symbol of Ukrainian resistance to foreign domination, placing him within the broader narrative of Eastern European national awakening.

Following the controversial defection of Hetman Ivan Mazepa to Charles XII of Sweden during the Great Northern War, and the subsequent execution of Hetman Pylyp Orlyk, the Russian Empire progressively curtailed the Hetmanate's autonomy. Polubotok, having served as a Polkovnyk (colonel) of Chernihiv, was elected Acting Hetman by the Cossack Starshyna (officer class) in 1722 after the death of Ivan Skoropadsky, but Peter the Great refused to confirm his election, fearing another independent-minded leader. Instead, the Tsar established the Little Russian Collegium, a Russian administrative body, to govern Ukraine, effectively bypassing the Hetmanate. Polubotok, however, continued to challenge Russian decrees, refusing to submit detailed financial accounts and petitioning for the restoration of Cossack rights and the election of a full Hetman, even traveling to Saint Petersburg with a delegation to present his grievances directly to the Tsar.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pavlo Polubotok's principled resistance to Peter the Great's imperial centralization, culminating in his death, significantly shaped the trajectory of Ukrainian autonomy within the Russian Empire and established him as an enduring symbol of national defiance. His actions directly contributed to heightened Russian control, but also inspired future generations of Ukrainian independence movements.
